applies_to: a project generated from the launch standard
status: PLAN - nothing in this file has been applied to GitHub or any other provider
why: ops/release/validate-workflows.mjs refuses any workflow whose name is not one of the canonical
ones, refuses production capability outside release.yml's canonical production jobs, pins the
canonical set with ops/release/workflow-templates.sha256 and pins the delivered digest manifest
and release policy against the standard that generated this project. None of that defends the
repository against someone who can commit anything to it: that person can edit the delivered
gate itself. D-014 puts the residual risk on branch protection and review, and this file is that
Apply it with the repository owner's authenticated identity before the first production release.

apply.how: Settings > Branches > Add branch ruleset, or the GitHub API with an identity that owns the repository. Record the application in the project's operation record; this file is a plan, not evidence.

workflow_validation.why: R5-03: the gate that enforces D-014 is the control the design's residual risk rests on, so it is a required check in its own right. It was previously excluded because ci.yml and release.yml shared the job id 'workflow-validation' and GitHub matches a required check by NAME.
workflow_validation.closed_by: R4-08: every job of ci.yml now carries the 'ci-' prefix, so no job id is shared between the two canonical workflows and every required check above names exactly one job.
workflow_validation.every_required_check_depends_on_it: In ci.yml every job needs ci-workflow-validation. In release.yml every required gate job needs workflow-validation, which needs record-candidate. A pull request whose workflow validation fails therefore has no green required check except record-candidate, and record-candidate alone does not satisfy this rule.

release_controls_self_test.why: R7REL-02: the delivered release CLIs used to be test-free in the only repository where they are the last line of defence, so a single line in a shared helper turned every one of them into a silent exit 0 with an empty log and a green pipeline. ops/release/release-controls.test.mjs runs every delivered CLI - and every project ops script - against a fixture it must refuse. R8REL-03: a green ci-release-controls used to be compatible with a self-test that had switched ITSELF off (one line: const installed = false, sixteen of seventeen cases skipped, exit 0). It is no longer the only guard: ops/release/check-project-scripts.mjs pins the self-test by digest and refuses a skipped, shortened, edited or deleted one, and that check runs in workflow-validation / ci-workflow-validation, which every other job needs. A neutered control now fails a required check even if this job is green.
release_controls_self_test.covers: validate-workflows, check-project-scripts, run-gate, secret-scan, required-gates, gate-results, evaluate-gates, decide-rollback, rollback-payload, health-outputs, record-candidate, record-promotion, check-promotion, select-staging-record, record-deployment, and the project ops scripts smoke, health, promote, rollback, render-migration and check-standard (R8REL-01). D-025: it also reads this project's own workflows and fails when a gate step is spelled as `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec vitest` or with a bare `--` separator instead of `node ops/release/run-gate.mjs <gate>`.

code_owner_review.why: R9REL-01/R9REL-02 (D-025): pnpm-workspace.yaml, .npmrc and .pnpmfile.cjs are listed although a managed project carries none of them - ops/release/run-gate.mjs refuses a gate in any repository that carries one the gate declaration does not name. Listing them here is the second half of the same rule: if one ever becomes legitimate it arrives as a reviewed diff. Three words in the first file (scriptShell: /usr/bin/true) turned every `pnpm run <gate>` into exit 0 with package.json byte-identical, and one vitest.config.js with passWithNoTests made a required gate green with zero tests executed; neither was a control by the previous predicate and neither touched a reviewed path. next.config.ts and .env.example are here because they are gate inputs a project really has. R7REL-01/R7REL-02: the delivered controls claim exactly two things - no downgrade is possible through DATA alone, and every code path a downgrade would need is under code-owner review. The second claim failed twice in the seventh review (ops/release/entrypoint.mjs was one line away from turning every release CLI into a silent exit 0 and was listed nowhere; a tree could be re-classified as 'the standard' by relocating delivered controls) and twice more in the eighth. The list is therefore whole DIRECTORIES plus the named configuration files the gates actually read. R8REL-01: ops/ - not ops/release/ - because the project's own ops scripts ARE gates (ops/render-migration.mjs is the migrations gate, ops/check-standard.mjs is operational_readiness) and the pre-promotion smoke, the post-promotion health, the promotion and the rollback all run from there; the previous entry covered none of them. R8REL-02: package.json, because `pnpm run <gate>` runs whatever that file says and one word there made the pre-promotion smoke gate vacuous with no diff in any reviewed path; pnpm-lock.yaml and tsconfig.json are here for the same reason (what --frozen-lockfile resolves, and what the typecheck gate checks), and eslint.config.mjs decides what the lint gate reports. .github/ - not .github/workflows/ - so dependabot.yml, which governs automated dependency pull requests, is covered too. .project-launch-starter.json covers templateVersion and releaseControlsSha256, and standard/ covers the only code that can put this repository into standard mode (standard/check-standard.mjs). R8REL-05: ops/release/release-controls.test.mjs now WALKS this repository and requires every file that is a control by nature - anything under .github/ or ops/, any executable module, any of the gate-configuration files above - to be covered by one of these entries. The previous derivation walked exactly the directories this list named, so it could not fail for the control that escaped them; this one fails for a new control anywhere in the tree. tests/browser/ holds the browser walk (Playwright configuration and tests) that the new-klus knob runs against the preview before a proefrit (roadmap 11H), so it is a quality gate too.
code_owner_review.how: A CODEOWNERS entry for these paths plus 'require review from Code Owners' on the ruleset. Not applied by this plan.

notes: enforce_admins true and empty bypass allowances are the point: a protection an administrator can
skip does not carry the residual risk D-014 assigns to it.
The production jobs (apply-migrations, production-build, smoke, promote-production,
post-promotion-health, rollback-app) and the branch-conditional jobs (staging-evidence,
tree-equivalence) run only on their own branch and are not listed as required checks:
they are the release itself, not a merge precondition. Protect them with the 'production'
GitHub environment (required reviewers and its own secrets), not with a branch rule.
The plan does not authorize destructive production data actions and grants no provider access.
